Close the account immediately without notice
Submit a suspicious transaction report
Take no action, because only UN and domestic lists matter
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 27.8.3 requires an STR where there is a positive name match with individuals or entities on other unilateral sanctions lists. The freezing duty attaches to the Domestic and UN lists.

quiz.question: Under the proliferation financing TFS, to whom does the bank immediately report a detection, freeze, block or rejection?
options: The Inspector-General of Police only
FIED, using the prescribed form
The Minister of Home Affairs only
The bank's external auditor
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 28.6.1 requires an immediate report to FIED on any detection, freezing, blocking or rejection. The additional report to the Inspector-General of Police is a feature of the terrorism-related regime in paragraph 27.

quiz.question: Farid's screening flags a customer with a common name. Data points partly match. Which step does BNM's policy document allow to help decide?
options: Asking the customer directly whether he is on the list
Clearing the alert if the customer has banked with the bank for years
Waiting for the next scheduled list update before deciding
Querying FIED on whether the customer is a specified entity
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 27.4.10 allows banks to direct queries to FIED in the case of similar or common names, alongside further inquiries required by paragraph 27.4.9.

quiz.question: Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia was penalised RM132,000 in 2026 even though no listed person had been onboarded. Why?
options: It froze an innocent customer's account by mistake
It failed to update its database without delay, so screening used outdated lists
It reported its matches to the police but never to FIED, and then closed the accounts without telling BNM
It refused to share screening records with BNM examiners
quiz.explanation: BNM found the bank did not update its sanctions database without delay after the Domestic List was published, so screening ran against outdated data. The duty is the process, whether or not a hit exists.

sessions.title: The Programme: Board, Compliance Officer, Training, Audit, Records and Enforcement
sessions.summary: Bring it together for the examination: governance, the Compliance Officer, employee screening, BNM's training rules, independent audit, record keeping and BNM's enforcement tools.
objectives: Distinguish the roles of the board, senior management and the Compliance Officer
Apply BNM's employee training rules in paragraph 11.6
Explain record-keeping periods and the independent audit requirements
Describe BNM's administrative, civil and publication powers under the amended AMLA

cards.title: The board asks for proof
cards.setting: Board Risk Committee room, head office. 2:00 pm.

lines.text: Nurul, BNM's examiners arrive next month. The committee wants to know one thing: could we prove our programme works, not just that it exists?
We can show the policy, the risk assessment and the reports. Training records are weaker: some new tellers served customers before finishing their AML module.
That is a requirement, not a nice-to-have, isn't it?
It is. Paragraph 11.6.5: customer-facing staff are trained before they deal with customers. And since March, section 19 duties bind people, not just the bank.
And the internal auditors want to see six years of records for a 2020 account that closed last year.
Then let's walk through the whole programme, the way an examiner would. Final stage: the Council Chamber.

cards.title: The compliance programme AMLA and BNM expect

scenes.heading: Governance
scenes.narration: Section 19 of AMLA requires internal programmes, policies, procedures and controls to guard against and detect offences. BNM adds that the programme must fit the bank's risks and size, under board oversight and senior management accountability.

scenes.heading: A Compliance Officer with weight
scenes.narration: Senior management appoints a Compliance Officer at management level at head office and designates one at each branch or subsidiary. The Compliance Officer must have stature, authority and seniority, and be fit and proper.

scenes.heading: Employee screening
scenes.narration: The bank evaluates employees' personal, employment and financial history when hiring and throughout employment, with clear triggers for re-screening.

scenes.heading: Training and awareness
scenes.narration: Training runs regularly with refreshers, fits each role, reaches customer-facing staff before they serve customers, and tells everyone they can be personally liable.

scenes.heading: Independent audit and records
scenes.narration: An independent audit tests whether the programme complies and works, and reports in writing to the board. Records are kept so any transaction can be rebuilt, for at least six years.

cards.title: Board and senior management: who does what
cards.caption: Paragraphs 11.2 and 11.3 of BNM's policy document.

items.label: Policies
items.left: Approves AML/CFT/CPF policies and minimum standards
items.right: Formulates policies and procedures and proposes updates

items.label: Oversight
items.right: Reports regularly on ML/TF/PF risk and control strength

items.label: Structure
items.left: Sets lines of authority and separates doers from controllers
items.right: Appoints the Compliance Officer and resources the programme

items.label: Audit
items.left: Ensures an effective, independent audit of AML/CFT/CPF
items.right: Makes sure issues raised are addressed in good time

items.label: People
items.left: Understands ML/TF/PF risks and required measures
items.right: Provides training at all levels and an employee assessment system

cards.title: BNM's training rules, paragraph by paragraph
cards.prompt: Match each paragraph of section 11.6 to what it requires or suggests.

pairs.right: Run awareness and training regularly, with refresher courses at appropriate intervals.
Make employees aware they may be held personally liable for failures.
Make AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures, and BNM's documents, available to all employees.
Pitch training to each employee's responsibilities and the bank's risks.
Train customer-facing employees before they deal with customers.
Guidance: train supervisors and managers on overall procedures and consequences of non-compliance.

cards.question: A teller joins the Penang branch on Monday. When must she complete AML/CFT/CPF training under BNM's policy document?
options: Within her first three months, at the next scheduled class
Before she deals with any customer
Within the first year, as part of annual refresher training
Only if her role involves opening accounts
cards.explanation: Paragraph 11.6.5 is a standard: employees who deal directly with customers must be trained on AML/CFT/CPF before dealing with the customer. A teller serves customers from day one, so training comes first.

cards.title: The Compliance Officer: BNM's minimum
cards.body:
BNM expects more of the Compliance Officer than a job title (paragraph 11.4):

- **Reference point** for AML/CFT/CPF across the bank, with enough **stature, authority and seniority** to influence decisions.
- **Fit and proper**: probity and integrity, competence, and financial integrity; with the knowledge to do the job and kept up to date. BNM encourages, but does not require, a relevant professional certification.
- **Clear, documented role**, covering compliance with the rules, CDD, records, ongoing due diligence, STRs and TFS, secure and confidential reporting channels, staff awareness and risks from new products and technology.
- **Notification**: the bank tells FIED in writing within **ten working days** of appointing or changing the Compliance Officer.

AMLA section 19 also requires compliance officers at management level in **each branch and subsidiary**.

cards.title: Whose job is it?
cards.prompt: Sort each duty to the role BNM's policy document gives it.

items.text: Approve the bank's AML/CFT/CPF policies, including CDD and TFS
Ensure regular independent audits and set their scope and frequency
Appoint a Compliance Officer at management level at head office
Provide appropriate AML/CFT/CPF training to employees at all levels
Allocate adequate resources to the programme
Evaluate internal suspicious transaction reports and submit STRs promptly
Ensure employees know the bank's reporting channels
Identify ML/TF/PF risks of new products and technology

cards.title: The life of an AML record
cards.caption: AMLA sections 13 and 17 and paragraph 24 of BNM's policy document. Breaching section 17 can bring a fine of up to RM3 million or five years' prison.

items.label: Capture
items.detail: CDD documents, verification results, transaction records and analysis, kept up to date.

items.label: Make it rebuildable
items.detail: Enough detail to reconstruct any transaction as evidence.

items.label: Keep at least six years
items.detail: Counted from account closure or the end of the relationship or transaction, whichever is later (AMLA s17).

items.label: Hold longer if needed
items.detail: Keep beyond six years while records are subject to investigation or prosecution, until told they are no longer needed.

items.label: Produce on demand
items.detail: In a form admissible under the Evidence Act 1950, available to supervisors and law enforcement in good time.

cards.title: What the auditors found
cards.setting: Internal audit close-out meeting, two weeks later.

lines.text: Audit's draft: sanctions screening is solid, but our STR review timeframes were never written into policy, and two branches have no designated compliance officer.
Both are standards. Paragraph 22.2.2 asks for a policy on review timeframes, and AMLA section 19 wants compliance officers in each branch.
And how often should audit look at AML at all? Some members want it every three years to save cost.
BNM leaves frequency to the board, but it must match the bank's ML/TF/PF risks, and any extra requirements BNM sets apply.

cards.title: Setting the audit plan
cards.situation: Seri Merbau Bank launched a fully digital account last year, its STR volumes doubled, and BNM took supervisory action against the bank two years ago for AML lapses. Some board members propose cutting the independent AML/CFT/CPF audit to once every three years and narrowing it to sanctions screening only. Dato' Lim asks you for a recommendation.

choices.text: Agree: sanctions screening is the highest-risk area, so audit only that, every three years.
choices.outcome: Poor. BNM sets a minimum scope: compliance with AMLA and instruments under it, internal policies, programme adequacy and effectiveness, and reporting and MIS reliability. Narrowing it breaches that minimum.

choices.text: Keep the full minimum scope and set frequency by risk; new channels, rising STR volumes and past enforcement all point to auditing more often, not less.
choices.outcome: Best. BNM's guidance lists exactly these circumstances as reasons to review audit frequency. The board decides, but it must be commensurate with the bank's risks.

choices.text: Keep the full scope every three years, but ask compliance to do yearly self-checks instead of audit.
choices.outcome: Partly reasonable: self-checks help, but they are not an independent audit. With these risk changes, three years is hard to justify.

choices.text: Leave the decision to the external auditors when they next visit.
choices.outcome: Poor. Paragraph 11.7 makes the board responsible for ensuring regular independent audits and for their scope and frequency.

cards.title: How BNM takes administrative action under AMLA s83B
steps: BNM is satisfied that a person has breached a relevant provision or instrument
BNM gives written notice of the proposed action and the grounds for it
The person may make written representations within fourteen days
BNM considers any representation and gives written notice of its decision
The decision takes effect, immediately or on the date BNM specifies
BNM may publish the action and its outcome in the public interest

cards.back: BNM may direct compliance, impose a monetary penalty of up to RM1 million, reprimand or issue a public statement, or require remedial measures.
BNM may direct or agree an action plan with a bank, director, officer or employee who failed to comply. Breaching it is an offence.

cards.front: Civil action and court orders (s83C, s83D)
cards.back: BNM may sue and seek orders, including removing a CEO, director or manager or barring them from management.
BNM may publish actions taken under AMLA and their outcomes, including settlements.
When a bank commits an offence, its directors and officers are deemed to have committed it unless they prove no consent or connivance and due diligence.
In proceedings for a Part IV offence, a person may show they took all reasonable steps and exercised due diligence.

cards.question: Customer records for an account closed in 2020 are part of a money laundering prosecution still under way. The six-year minimum has ended. What should the bank do?
options: Destroy them, because the retention period has ended
Hand them to the customer, since the account is closed
Keep them only if the customer consents
Keep them until the law enforcement agency says they are no longer needed
cards.explanation: Paragraph 24.4 requires records under ongoing investigation or prosecution to be kept beyond the retention period until the relevant law enforcement agency confirms they are no longer required. Destroying them early would also defeat the duty to make records available to law enforcement in a timely manner.

cards.title: Real cases: what banks fixed after BNM acted
cards.body:
BNM's enforcement notices name the **root causes** behind penalties, and the same fixes keep appearing:

- **SME Bank (2025, RM460,000):** late STRs due to inadequate staff awareness; fixed with stronger policies and **enhanced staff training**.
- **HSBC Bank Malaysia (2025, RM324,000):** lack of understanding of beneficial owner rules; fixed with better monitoring and **refresher training**.
- **AEON Credit Service (2026, RM520,000):** sanctions failures due to lack of staff oversight and an SOP gap; fixed with a better SOP and **refresher training**.
- **AmBank (M) (2026, RM276,000):** late CTRs after **system changes** with weak oversight; fixed with stronger systems, SOPs and oversight.

In every notice BNM weighed reasonable care, past record and remediation, and gave credit for self-reporting where it applied.

**The lesson:** training, procedures and change control are the three levers examiners test.

cards.title: Exam-readiness checklist for your own role
cards.body:
Before the examiners arrive, make sure you can:

- Show your **training record**, completed before you served customers if you are customer-facing.
- Find the bank's **AML/CFT/CPF policy and procedures** without help.
- Explain your **escalation route** for suspicion and for sanctions hits.
- Retrieve a **customer file** and rebuild a transaction from the records.
- Say in one sentence why you may be **personally liable**.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: AMLA section 19 requires a compliance programme with employee screening, ongoing training and independent audit; since March 2026 it binds directors, officers and employees too.
The board approves policies and oversees; senior management implements, resources, appoints the Compliance Officer and provides training.
The Compliance Officer must be senior and fit and proper; FIED is told within ten working days of any appointment or change.
Customer-facing staff must be trained before dealing with customers, and all staff told they may be personally liable.
Records are kept at least six years, longer when under investigation, in a form admissible in court.
BNM can impose penalties up to RM1 million, reprimand, publish, require action plans and seek court orders.

cards.prompt: If a BNM examiner sat with you for ten minutes tomorrow, which part of your work would you be least comfortable explaining? What will you do this week to fix that?

quiz.question: Under AMLA section 19, which three elements must a reporting institution's compliance programme include?
options: Employee integrity screening, ongoing training and an independent audit function
Customer satisfaction surveys, staff bonuses and a hotline
External legal opinions, professional indemnity insurance cover and a media and press relations policy
Annual board retreats, IT upgrades and a code of dress
quiz.explanation: Section 19(2) lists procedures for employee integrity and history checks, ongoing employee training including KYC, and an independent audit function.

quiz.question: Within how many working days must FIED be told in writing that the bank has appointed a new Compliance Officer?
options: Two working days
Five working days
Ten working days
Thirty working days
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.4.9 requires written notice to FIED within ten working days of the appointment or change, with contact details.

quiz.question: A new contact centre agent will handle customer calls from her second day. When must her AML/CFT/CPF training happen?
options: Within her first quarter
Before she deals with any customer
At the next annual refresher
Only after her probation period ends
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.6.5 requires employees who deal directly with customers to be trained before dealing with the customer.

quiz.question: Which body is responsible under BNM's policy document for ensuring regular independent audits of AML/CFT/CPF measures?
options: The Compliance Officer
The branch managers
The external auditor alone
The board
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.7.2 places this on the board, which also sets the frequency and scope in line with the bank's risks.

quiz.question: The board proposes an AML/CFT/CPF audit every three years even though the bank launched new digital channels and STR volumes doubled. What does BNM's guidance suggest?
options: Three years is BNM's fixed minimum frequency for every bank, so the proposal is acceptable
These changes are reasons to review frequency upwards in line with risk
Audit frequency is the Compliance Officer's decision alone
New channels reduce the need for audit because they are automated
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.7.6 lists new products or channels and changes in reporting volumes as circumstances to consider when setting audit frequency, which must match the risks.

quiz.question: How long must records obtained in CDD be kept under BNM's policy document?
options: At least five years after account opening
At least seven years after the last statement was sent
At least three years after the customer's death
At least six years after the transaction or the end of the relationship
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 24.3 sets at least six years following completion of the transaction, termination of the relationship or the date of the occasional transaction. AMLA section 17 also sets six years.

quiz.question: Records for a closed account are subject to an ongoing police investigation, and six years have passed. What must the bank do?
options: Keep them until the agency says they are no longer required
Destroy them under the normal retention schedule
Return them to the former customer
Keep them for one more year and then destroy them securely
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 24.4 requires retention beyond the stipulated period while records are subject to investigation or prosecution, until the agency confirms they are no longer needed.

quiz.question: BNM proposes administrative action against a bank officer under section 83B of AMLA. What opportunity must he be given?
options: To appeal directly to the Federal Court within seven days of the notice
To pay a compound instead within thirty days
To make written representations within fourteen days of the notice
To choose a different regulator to hear the case
quiz.explanation: Section 83B requires written notice of the proposed action and grounds, and gives the person fourteen days to make written representations before a decision.

quiz.question: A bank commits an AMLA offence. A director says he cannot be charged because he never personally acted. What does section 87 provide?
options: He cannot be charged unless the bank itself is convicted first, and only if he signed the board minutes approving the breach
He is liable only if he signed the relevant document
He is deemed to have committed it unless he proves no consent or connivance and due diligence
He is automatically liable with no defence available
quiz.explanation: Section 87 deems directors and officers to have committed the offence unless they prove it happened without their consent or connivance and they exercised due diligence. The bank need not be convicted first.

quiz.question: Which of these is a duty of the Compliance Officer under paragraph 11.4.8?
options: Ensure internal STRs are evaluated before being promptly reported to FIED
Approve the bank's AML/CFT/CPF policies on behalf of the board of directors
Set the scope and frequency of the independent audit
Appoint compliance officers in each branch on behalf of the board
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.4.8(g) gives the Compliance Officer the duty to ensure internal STRs are evaluated before prompt reporting to FIED. Policy approval and audit scope sit with the board.

regulators: Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department, BNM (FIED)

bank.question: Which statement best describes how AMLA and BNM's AML/CFT/CPF and TFS policy document relate for a licensed bank?
options: AMLA sets the offences and core duties; the policy document, issued under AMLA and other Acts, sets detailed binding standards
The policy document replaced AMLA for licensed banks when it took effect in February 2024, so AMLA now only governs non-bank reporting institutions
AMLA applies only to criminals, while the policy document applies only to banks
The two are alternatives, and a bank may choose which one to follow
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4 of the policy document says it is issued under AMLA sections including 13 to 19 and 83, and under the FSA and other Acts. AMLA remains the base law; the policy document fills in the detail.

bank.question: Under the amended section 19 of AMLA, who can commit an offence by failing to implement the compliance programme the Act requires?
options: Only the board of directors, collectively
Only the Compliance Officer appointed at head office and notified to FIED in writing
The reporting institution, or any of its directors, officers or employees
Only the chief executive officer named in the licence
bank.explanation: Act A1761 inserted directors, officers and employees into section 19 and created an offence with a fine of up to RM1 million for contraventions.

bank.question: A director asks what the maximum fine is for breaching section 19 of AMLA after March 2026. What is the correct answer?
options: RM100,000 per breach
RM3 million
RM1 million
RM5 million
bank.explanation: New section 19(8) sets a fine not exceeding RM1 million. RM3 million applies to tipping off and record retention offences; RM5 million is the floor option for the money laundering fine.

bank.question: Before Act A1761, section 22 of AMLA required officers to take reasonable steps to ensure compliance and allowed BNM to agree action plans. What happened to it?
options: It was deleted, and new section 83A now provides for directed or agreed action plans
It was kept unchanged and extended to proliferation financing
It was moved into the BNM policy document as a G paragraph, so that it now operates only as guidance for officers of reporting institutions
It was replaced by a duty on customers to report suspicion
bank.explanation: Act A1761 deleted section 22. New section 83A lets the competent authority direct or agree an action plan with an institution or its directors, officers or employees; failing to comply is an offence.

bank.question: A money launderer moved RM2 million of crime proceeds through accounts. If convicted under section 4 of AMLA as amended, what is the minimum fine?
options: RM2 million: the value of the proceeds involved, since a fine cannot exceed the proceeds
RM5 million: the fixed statutory fine in every case
RM1 million: the general penalty under section 86
RM10 million: five times the proceeds, as that exceeds RM5 million
bank.explanation: Section 4 sets a fine of not less than five times the proceeds or RM5 million, whichever is higher. Five times RM2 million is RM10 million, which is higher. Imprisonment of up to fifteen years also applies.

bank.question: A customer splits RM60,000 of cash into several smaller deposits across days to avoid a reporting requirement. Which AMLA offence is most directly engaged?
options: Tipping off, under section 14A
Structuring transactions to evade reporting, under section 4A
Falsifying documents, under section 89
Opening or operating an account in a false name, under section 18
bank.explanation: Section 4A forbids structuring transactions to avoid the reporting requirement in section 14(1)(a), with a fine of up to five times the aggregate value or up to seven years' prison, or both.

bank.question: Under section 83E inserted by Act A1761, what may BNM do with information about enforcement actions?
options: Publish actions taken under AMLA and their outcomes, including settlements, in the public interest
Only share them privately with the bank's external auditors
Publish them only after a court conviction is final and every appeal has been exhausted by the person concerned
Keep them secret under AMLA's secrecy provisions
bank.explanation: Section 83E lets the competent authority, the regulatory or supervisory authority or an enforcement agency publish actions taken under the Act, including compounds, civil and administrative actions, and their outcomes.

bank.question: Which court order may BNM seek under new section 83D of AMLA against a bank's chief executive officer who has contravened the Act?
options: An order cancelling his professional qualifications worldwide
An order transferring all of his shares in the bank to Bank Negara Malaysia
An order removing him from office or barring him from management for a set period
An order requiring him to serve as Compliance Officer
bank.explanation: Section 83D(1)(ff) allows the court to remove a CEO, director or manager, or bar them from being one or from management of the institution for a period the court decides.

bank.question: Paragraph 9.1 of BNM's policy document refers to enforcement and supervisory action. Against whom can such action be taken for breaching S provisions?
options: Only the reporting institution as a company
The reporting institution, including its directors, officers and employees
Only customers who give false information to the bank during onboarding
Only the external auditors who sign off the accounts
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.1 states that enforcement and/or supervisory action can be taken against the reporting institution, including its directors, officers and employees, for non-compliance with S provisions.

bank.question: A Malaysian sole trader wants to open a current account. The RM collects all CDD data but cannot verify the address until a utility bill arrives in a week. The customer is low risk with no suspicion. What may the bank do?
options: Refuse the account until every document has been verified, as delayed verification is never permitted in Malaysia
Open the account and verify at the first annual review
Open the account and skip address verification entirely
Open with risk controls such as limits, and complete verification within ten working days
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 14A.10.5 to 14A.10.9 allow delayed verification for low risk with no suspicion, where the delay is essential and risks are managed, for example by limiting transactions, and normally within ten working days.

bank.question: A private company's only shareholder is a trust. The trust's trustee is a corporate trust company. Who must the bank try to identify as beneficial owners?
options: Only the corporate trust company
The trust's settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries and other controllers
Only the company's directors, since a trust cannot own a company
Nobody, because trusts are exempt from beneficial owner rules
bank.explanation: For legal arrangements the policy document lists settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries and others with ultimate effective control, and says that where a party is a legal person its own beneficial owner should be identified.

bank.question: Which customer category is exempted from the bank obtaining its certificate of incorporation and verifying its directors and shareholders, while the bank still records their identities?
options: A private limited company with fewer than five shareholders
A foreign company listed on any exchange in a higher-risk country
A newly registered society or charity
A public company listed on Bursa Malaysia
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14A.9.8 exempts listed companies on Bursa Malaysia, among others, but paragraph 14A.9.9 still requires the bank to identify and keep director and shareholder information. Foreign listed companies in higher-risk countries are not exempt.

bank.question: A domestic PEP's relationship is assessed as not higher risk. Which treatment does BNM allow?
options: CDD measures similar to other customers, with the risk assessment documented
Enhanced CDD with head office senior management approval in every case, whatever the assessment shows
No CDD at all, because the customer is a public figure
A ban on opening any account for domestic PEPs
bank.explanation: Paragraph 15.3.5 allows CDD similar to other customers for domestic PEPs not assessed as higher risk. Enhanced measures are required if the assessment shows higher risk.

bank.question: Which person is a 'family member' of a PEP under BNM's definition?
options: The PEP's former classmate
The PEP's neighbour
The PEP's spouse's parent
The PEP's family lawyer
bank.explanation: BNM lists parent, sibling, spouse, child and spouse's parent. A family lawyer or former classmate may need the close associate test, which looks at social or professional closeness.

bank.question: The FATF calls on members to apply enhanced due diligence to a country. A customer is from that country. What does paragraph 17 require of Seri Merbau Bank?
options: Closing every account linked to the country at once and reporting each one to FIED as an STR
Standard CDD, because country lists are only advisory
Enhanced CDD proportionate to the risk, including any specific measures the FATF or the Government imposes
Reporting every transaction of the customer to FIED as an STR
bank.explanation: Paragraph 17.1 and 17.2 require enhanced CDD, proportionate to risk, for persons from higher-risk countries called for by the FATF or the Government, including any specific measures imposed. Countermeasures apply when called for.

bank.question: A bank relies on a group company to introduce customers and perform CDD. Which task can it NEVER pass to the third party?
options: Ongoing due diligence on the customers
Collecting identity documents at onboarding
Introducing new business to the bank
Verifying the customer's identity at onboarding
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.9 says reporting institutions shall not rely on third parties to conduct ongoing due diligence. Reliance for initial CDD and introductions is possible under conditions.

bank.question: Under paragraph 10.6, which set of factors must a customer risk profile consider?
options: Customer age, gender and religion only
Account balance, fee income, relationship length and the customer's credit score only
Only the risk rating given by another bank
Customer, country, and product, service or channel risk, plus other risk signs
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.6.2 lists customer risk, country or geographical risk, products, services, transactions or delivery channels, and any other information suggesting higher risk.

bank.question: A bank plans to launch a new instant-payment wallet. When must it assess the ML/TF/PF risks of the product?
options: Within six months after launch, once enough transaction data exists to assess
Before the launch, and then take measures to manage the risks
Only if BNM asks for an assessment
Only if the product handles cash
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.2 requires a risk assessment prior to the launch or use of new products, practices and technologies, and appropriate measures to manage and mitigate the risks.

bank.question: BNM's paragraph 22.1.1 lists situations where an STR must be submitted. Which of these is one of them?
options: The transaction has no clear economic purpose
The customer is a foreign national
The transaction exceeds RM10,000 in value
The customer pays a higher fee than usual
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22.1.1 covers transactions that appear unusual, have no clear economic purpose, appear illegal, involve proceeds of unlawful activity or instrumentalities of an offence, or indicate ML/TF/PF, regardless of amount.

bank.question: A branch manager tells Daniel to hold back an internal report until the customer's loan is fully drawn, so as not to 'disrupt' a good relationship. What should Daniel do?
options: Wait until the loan is fully drawn down, because the branch manager outranks him and owns the customer relationship
Ask the customer whether the funds are legitimate
Channel the report to the Compliance Officer without delay, as the reporting mechanism requires
Delete the report and note the manager's instruction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22.2.1 makes the branch compliance officer responsible for channelling all internal reports to the Compliance Officer, and STRs must be prompt. A commercial reason never justifies delay.

bank.question: Which requirement applies to how Seri Merbau Bank handles internal STRs that the Compliance Officer decides NOT to submit?
options: Destroy them after thirty days to protect customer privacy and avoid holding unnecessary personal data
Keep them, with supporting evidence, in a complete file available to supervisors on request
Return them to the employees who raised them
Forward them to the customer's relationship manager
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22.4 requires the Compliance Officer to maintain a complete file of all internal STRs and supporting evidence, whether submitted or not, and to make them available to supervisors on request.

bank.question: A customer deposits RM18,000 cash, then withdraws RM8,000 cash from the same account on the same day, and the teller has no concerns. A week later the bank finds no report was filed. Which duty was breached?
options: Nothing, because the net cash amount moved that day was only RM10,000
The STR, which was due within one working day
The duty to freeze, which applies to large cash
The cash threshold report, which was due within five working days
bank.explanation: Deposits and withdrawals are aggregated, not offset: RM26,000 reaches the RM25,000 threshold. The CTR was due within five working days. No suspicion arose, so no STR was due.

bank.question: Seri Merbau Bank wants to share details of an STR with its overseas parent bank for group risk management. Under AMLA section 14A and paragraph 23, what is the safest route?
options: Share freely, because the parent is part of the same banking group and needs the information for group risk management
Apply in writing to the Director of FIED for authorisation, with justification and safeguards
Share only the customer's name, which is not report information
Ask the customer to consent to the disclosure
bank.explanation: The related corporation exception in s14A(3)(b) covers companies incorporated in Malaysia and engaged in financial services in Malaysia. For other disclosure, paragraph 23.4 lets the bank seek written authorisation from FIED's Director.

bank.question: Which statement about the Compliance Officer's discretion to file STRs is correct under BNM's policy document?
options: The CEO must approve each STR before it is submitted to FIED, after legal review by the bank's counsel
The board must ratify each STR at its next meeting
The branch manager decides for branch customers
The Compliance Officer has sole discretion and independence to report suspicious transactions
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22.2.7 gives the Compliance Officer sole discretion and independence to report, and requires utmost confidentiality.

bank.question: BNM's Appendix 4a lists transactions that may trigger suspicion. Which of these is listed?
options: Multiple cash deposits by machine up to daily limits to avoid CDD at the counter
A customer who always uses the same branch and the same teller for all of her cash deposits
A salary account receiving a regular monthly credit
A customer who asks for a printed statement each month
bank.explanation: Appendix 4a includes multiple cash deposits or withdrawals via cash deposit machines up to the daily limit to avoid CDD verification over the counter. Regular, explained activity is not a trigger.

bank.question: After filing an STR, the Compliance Officer receives a request from FIED for more documents. What does the policy document require?
options: Refuse, because the customer has not consented
Provide it only after a court order is served on the bank
Provide the additional information and respond promptly
Ask the customer to send the documents directly
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22.2.8 requires banks to provide additional information and documents FIED requests and to respond promptly to further enquiries about reports under section 14 of AMLA.

bank.question: Under the amended section 14 of AMLA, which new ground for reporting did Act A1761 add?
options: Any foreign currency transaction above RM10,000, whether or not there is any suspicion about it at all
Any transaction by a politically exposed person
Suspicion that a transaction, activity or property is linked to a restricted activity or proliferator
Any account opened without face-to-face contact
bank.explanation: Act A1761 added section 14(1)(d), covering suspicion of links to restricted activity, proliferators or persons financing restricted activity, and (e) for activity the competent authority specifies.

bank.question: Which minimum data points does BNM require banks to obtain to facilitate sanctions screening, even for transactions below CDD thresholds?
options: Full name, NRIC or passport number, and date of birth
Full name, occupation and monthly income from employment
Mobile number, email address and home address
Nationality, employer and purpose of transaction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27.4.3 requires at least full name, NRIC or passport or other official document number, and date of birth to facilitate screening.

bank.question: A listing is published on the UN website on a Friday evening. Seri Merbau Bank's vendor updates the screening database on Tuesday. What is the compliance issue?
options: None, because outsourced screening vendors are allowed five working days to update the lists
None, because UN lists apply only after the Gazette
None, if no matching customer is eventually found
The database must be updated without delay upon publication, not days later
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27.3.2 requires updates without delay upon publication on the UN website. BNM penalised Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia in 2026 for screening against an outdated database even though no listed person was onboarded.

bank.question: A company customer is not listed, but its 60% owner has just been added to the Domestic List. What should the bank consider?
options: Nothing, because only the listed person's own accounts matter
Whether the company is a related party, as its funds may be owned or controlled by a specified entity
Closing the company account immediately without any further analysis or recording of reasons for the decision
Asking the listed owner to sell his shares before acting
bank.explanation: A related party includes a person whose funds are wholly or jointly owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by a specified entity. Paragraph 27.5 requires due diligence on related parties and analysis of past transactions.

bank.question: How long does a freeze under the terrorism-related TFS remain in effect?
options: Until the specified entity is removed from the Domestic List or UNSCR List
For ninety days only, after which the bank must apply to the Minister to extend it
Until the customer provides a satisfactory explanation
Until the Compliance Officer decides to lift it
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27.6.3 keeps the freeze or block in effect until the entity is delisted as published by the UN or in the Gazette.

bank.question: Zurich General Insurance Malaysia was penalised RM1.04 million in 2026. Which failure did BNM identify besides outdated screening?
options: Failing to submit cash threshold reports on large cash premiums paid at its branches
Failing to appoint a Compliance Officer at head office
Failing to freeze a specified entity's funds and report to BNM immediately
Failing to keep records for six years
bank.explanation: BNM's notice found Zurich failed to update its database without delay, failed to resolve potential matches, and failed to freeze one specified entity's funds and report to BNM immediately.

bank.question: A customer of Seri Merbau Bank is confirmed as a specified entity. Two weeks after the immediate report, the frozen balance receives interest. What further reporting applies?
options: None, because the immediate report to FIED and the police covers everything that follows
Periodic reporting of changes to the frozen funds, in the form and intervals BNM specifies
A new STR every time interest is credited
A report to the customer explaining the interest
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27.7.2 requires banks holding frozen funds to report changes to those funds using the form and at the intervals in Appendix 8b.

bank.question: A bank's PF risk assessment rates its institutional PF risk as low. What does BNM say about applying TFS on proliferation financing?
options: Low PF risk allows the bank to screen only quarterly
Low PF risk means PF sanctions screening becomes optional for the bank
Low PF risk allows freezing to wait for police instructions
TFS on PF must be fully implemented whatever the institutional PF risk level
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.5.2 requires full implementation of TFS on PF irrespective of the institutional PF risk level. Lower risk affects other mitigation measures, not the sanctions duties.

bank.question: Under BNM's paragraph 10.4, what does 'PF risk' mean for a bank's PF risk assessment?
options: The risk that any customer trades in any dual-use goods at all, anywhere in the world
The risk of breach, non-implementation or evasion of the targeted financial sanctions on PF
The risk of the bank's own staff joining a weapons programme
The risk of currency losses on trade finance transactions
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.4.1 limits PF risk, for this purpose, to potential breach, non-implementation or evasion of the TFS on PF in paragraph 28.

bank.question: In 2025 BNM penalised HSBC's two Malaysian banking entities about RM2.9 million for sanctions screening failures. What made BNM's notice especially critical?
options: A listed terrorist moved large sums through the bank's accounts undetected for several years
The bank refused to cooperate with BNM's examiners
The bank reported its screening matches to a foreign regulator only
Customers were onboarded without proper screening, and the breach recurred after remediation
bank.explanation: BNM noted staff oversight, ineffective maker-checker functions and system gaps, and that remedial measures were insufficient so the breach recurred in 2024. No specified entity was onboarded.

bank.question: Under BNM's paragraph 11.5, when must a bank's employee screening apply?
options: On hiring and throughout employment, with clear triggers for re-screening
Only on hiring, and only for customer-facing roles such as tellers and relationship managers
Only after an employee is suspected of fraud
Only for staff who earn above a salary threshold
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.5.3 applies screening on hiring and throughout employment, and paragraph 11.5.4 requires evaluation of criminal, employment and financial history plus clear re-screening triggers.

bank.question: A bank's AML training is identical for tellers, trade finance officers and board members. Which BNM standard does that most likely fail?
options: Training must be delivered by an external provider approved in advance by Bank Negara Malaysia
Training must be completed in a single annual session
Training must be appropriate to each employee's level of responsibility and the bank's risks
Training must be identical for every employee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.6.4 requires training appropriate to employees' responsibilities in detecting ML/TF/PF and to the risks the bank has identified. Paragraph 11.6.7 suggests role-specific content.

bank.question: What minimum scope does BNM set for the independent AML/CFT/CPF audit?
options: Only a sample check of sanctions screening alerts
Only a review of the Compliance Officer's qualifications
AMLA and policy compliance, programme effectiveness and reporting reliability
Only the financial statements of the bank
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.7.5 sets the minimum scope: compliance with AMLA and instruments under it, internal policies, adequacy and effectiveness of the programme, and reliability, integrity and timeliness of reporting and MIS.

bank.question: Who must receive the auditor's written report on the effectiveness of AML/CFT/CPF measures?
options: The board
The customer complaints unit
The Securities Commission
Each branch manager
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.7.8 requires the auditor to submit a written report to the board, and findings and corrective measures must be available to FIED on request.

bank.question: Which statement about record retention is correct under AMLA as amended?
options: Records are kept for at least five years from the date of account opening only
Records may be destroyed once a CTR has been filed
Records need to be kept only for customers rated high risk
At least six years from closure or completion, whichever is later
bank.explanation: Section 17(1), as amended by Act A1761, sets at least six years from the account closing or the business relationship, transaction or activity being completed or terminated, whichever is later.

bank.question: A bank officer is found to have repeatedly ignored the bank's AML procedures. Which BNM tool under the amended AMLA could apply to him personally, without a criminal trial?
options: Imprisonment ordered by BNM's FIED
An administrative monetary penalty under section 83B, after notice and a chance to respond
Forfeiture of his family house under the money laundering offence in section 4
A ban from banking imposed by the bank's auditors
bank.explanation: Section 83B lets the competent or supervisory authority take administrative action, including penalties up to RM1 million, against 'any person' who breaches Part IV duties, which now bind officers and employees.

bank.question: Senior management at Seri Merbau Bank wants to cut AML training to save costs. Which of their duties under paragraph 11.3.2 does this put at risk?
options: Providing appropriate levels of AML/CFT/CPF training for employees at all levels
Approving the bank's dividend policy and capital plan each financial year
Setting the bank's interest rates on deposits
Appointing the bank's external statutory auditor
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.3.2(h) makes senior management responsible for providing appropriate levels of training for employees at all levels, and 11.3.2(f) for allocating adequate resources.

bank.question: BNM's enforcement notices in 2025 and 2026 repeatedly cited refresher training as a remedy. What is the best conclusion for a bank's programme?
options: Training is a cosmetic remedy that BNM accepts instead of imposing any monetary penalty on the bank
Training matters only for banks that have already been penalised
Gaps in staff knowledge are a common root cause of breaches, so training is a core control
Training can replace system controls such as screening
bank.explanation: Notices for SME Bank, HSBC, AEON Credit and Zurich cited awareness or oversight gaps and listed training among remedies. Training does not replace controls or avoid penalties, but it addresses a recurring cause.
